It was shaped by the new Greek social elite. It was shaped by external artistic influences as well. These influences came predominantly from Germany and France.

Sculpture and painting

19th century

The School of Munich

Modern Greek art began to be developed around the time of Romanticism. Greek artists absorbed many elements. They absorbed these elements from their European colleagues. This resulted in the culmination of the distinctive style of Greek Romantic art. This art was inspired by revolutionary ideals. This art was inspired by the country's geography and history as well. Centuries of Ottoman rule had occurred. Few opportunities existed for an education in the arts. These opportunities existed in the newly independent Greece. So studying abroad was imperative for artists. Munich was an important international center for the arts at that time. It was the place. The majority of the Greek artists of the 19th century chose to study there. The school of Munich existed. Karl von Piloty led it. True fresco was taught there. It was taught for mural paintings on fresh wet lime plaster. Much of the art was emotional during this period. Much of the art was theatrical in tone. The most prominent themes existed. These themes belonged to the school of Munich. These themes were urban life. These themes were rural life. These themes were still life. These themes were landscape.

Later on, they would return to Greece. They would pass on their knowledge. Some of them remained in Munich. This was the so-called Athens on the Isar. Both academic bonds developed. Personal bonds developed between early Greek painters and Munich artistry. This gave birth to the Greek "Munich School" of painting. Nikolaos Gysis was an important teacher. He was an artist at the Munich Academy. He soon became a leading figure among Greek artists. Academism existed. Realism existed. Genre painting existed. Upper middle class portraiture existed. Still life existed. Landscape painting existed. These often represented impressionist features. They would be replaced in the end of the 19th century by Symbolism. They would be replaced by Jugendstil. They would be replaced by Art Nouveau. These are mainly traced in the work of Nikolaos Gysis. These are mainly traced in the work of Aristeas and others. Early-20th-century modernism is also represented by significant Greek artists in Munich. Many of these Munich School artists chose subjects. These subjects included everyday Greek life. These subjects included local customs. These subjects included living conditions. Several important painters emerged at this time. Theodoros Vryzakis specialized in historical painting. He was especially inspired by the 1821 Greek War of Independence. Nikiphoros Lytras concentrated on realistic depictions. These were depictions of Greek life. Georgios Jakobides devoted his attention to infants and children. He would later become the first Director. He directed the new National Gallery of Athens. Georgios Roilos was another leading painter of the period. He was closely associated with the Munich School. This was especially true in his early career. Konstantinos Volanakis was inspired mostly. He was inspired by the Greek sea.

Other artists were associated with the School of Munich. These artists were Symeon Sabbides. These artists were Yannoulis Chalepas. These artists were Leonidas Drosis. Quite a few modernist artists studied in Munich as well. These artists included Theofrastos Triantafyllidis. These artists included Jorgos Busianis. These artists also included Giorgio de Chirico.

Notable sculptors existed. They worked for the new Greek Kingdom. These sculptors were Leonidas Drosis. His major work was the extensive neo-classical architectural ornament at the Academy of Athens. These sculptors were Lazaros Sochos. These sculptors were Georgios Vitalis. These sculptors were Dimitrios Filippotis. These sculptors were Ioannis Kossos. These sculptors were Yannoulis Chalepas. These sculptors were Georgios Bonanos. These sculptors were Lazaros Fytalis.

The School of Paris

A few Greek painters studied in Paris. They resided in the French capital. They followed the guidelines of the French Art Academy. They invariably had their own interpretations. Jacob Rizos was involved with the rendering of female grace. Theodoros Rallis was involved with scenes from the Orthodox East. Nikolaos Xydias Typaldos was involved with portraiture. He was involved with still life. He was involved with genre painting. The avant-garde Impressionist movement developed during this period in Paris. But most Greek painters remained faithful. They remained faithful to the precepts of their teachers. They made only some nebulous thrusts in the direction of this movement. The first Greek impressionist was Périclès Pantazis. He settled in Belgium after Paris. He became a part of the avant-garde group Circle de la pâte.

Themes-artistic depictions

Many Greek artists of this period also drew upon El Greco's style. They drew upon it for inspiration. They did this particularly when creating art. This art was based on religious themes. This tied in with the idea of modern secular Greek art of the period. This art referenced more classical styles. Religious art referenced Byzantine styles. Religious art referenced Byzantine inspired art. Moreover, an important role was played. An often pioneering role was played by artists from Ionian islands in the 18th century. They played this role in the beginning of the 19th century. They exploited conquests of the Italian Renaissance. They exploited conquests of baroque ateliers. Efforts persisted with new directions and objectives. Greek artists emerged. They emerged in the world during the first decades of the 19th century. They reconnected Greek art with its ancient tradition. They reconnected Greek art with the quests of the European ateliers as well. They especially reconnected with those of the Munich School. Defining examples of the Greek contemporary art of the period existed. These included the works of Theodoros Vryzakis. These included the works of Nikiphoros Lytras.

20th century

Landscape painting held sway at the beginning of the 20th century. The interest of painters turned toward the study of light and color. The dependence of Munich slackened. Paris became the pole of attraction. It became this for the artists of the period. Demetrios Galanis achieved wide recognition in France in the early 20th century. He was a contemporary of Picasso. He was a friend of Picasso. He achieved lifelong membership of the Académie française. This followed his acclaim by the critic Andre Malreaux. Malreaux acclaimed him as an artist. This artist was capable "of stirring emotions as powerful as those of Giotto". Nikos Engonopoulos achieved international recognition later in the century. "No Wedding Bells for Him" is a short story. P. G. Wodehouse wrote it. He is a British author. The story first appeared in the United States. It was in the October 1923 issue of Cosmopolitan. It appeared in the United Kingdom later. It was in the November 1923 Strand. It features Stanley Featherstonehaugh Ukridge. Ukridge is irrepressible. The story was included in the collection Ukridge. That collection was published in 1924.

Plot
Ukridge and Corky run into a friend. The friend belongs to Ukridge. He is a chauffeur. He drives a shiny new Daimler. He offers to take them for a ride. They go along the way. A creditor of Ukridge's sees them. They shake him off. They almost hit a young girl. Ukridge insists on something. They must drive her to her home. Her home is near Clapham Common. He befriends her family. The family is impressed. They are impressed by the car. They are impressed by Ukridge's famous Aunt Julia.

Corky meets Ukridge a week later. They meet in the British Museum. Two children accompany him. He reveals something. He has been visiting the house. He goes there mainly for the free food. He promises to take the family out on trips. He will use his friend's car. They believe the car to be his. He promises to introduce them to his aunt. He reveals something else. She has disowned him. A letter states this. The letter says "from now on, I have no nephew".

Corky returns from short holiday. George Tupper tells him something. Ukridge is engaged. Corky visits his friend. He finds him with a black eye. He hears the tale. Ukridge found himself inadvertently engaged. The girl is from Clapham Common. A rival suitor punched him. The rival suitor is named Finch. They talk on Ukridge's doorstep. The creditor from the car ride arrives. Ukridge hides. A friendly passer-by does something. He soothes the enraged creditor. He argues something. He knows where Ukridge lives. Ukridge moves out of his house. He remarks on the good fortune. It led him to use the pseudonym "Mr. Smallweed". He used it when dealing with the man.

Ukridge and Corky form a plot. The plot will get Ukridge out of the engagement. They will feign ill-health. Corky is delivering his speech to the family. The passer-by arrives. He is George Finch. He is Ukridge's rival for the girl. He reveals something. Ukridge is an impoverished imposter. He is in fact called Smallweed. Finch produces the creditor. This proves it. He also bears a letter. The letter is from Ukridge's aunt. She claims she has no nephew. Corky has paid off the debt. He pays it to the creditor. The two are chased from the house.

Main characters
Stanley Featherstonehaugh Ukridge is the irrepressible entrepreneur. Julia Ukridge is his haughty writer aunt. Jimmy Corcoran is Ukridge's writer friend. George Tupper is an old schoolfriend. He is a schoolfriend of Ukridge and Corcoran. Frederick is a chauffeur. He is a friend of Ukridge. Mabel Price is a girl. Ukridge meets her on the road. Mr Price is her doting father. Ernie Finch is her admirer. He is a resourceful man. Mr Grindlay is a man. Ukridge owes money to him. He knows him only as "Mr Smallweed".

Publication history
The story was illustrated. T. D. Skidmore illustrated it in Cosmopolitan. Reginald Cleaver illustrated it in the Strand.

"No Wedding Bells for Him" was included in the 1932 collection Nothing But Wodehouse. Ogden Nash edited it. Doubleday, Doran & Company published it. It was included in Week-End Wodehouse. That is the UK edition. Herbert Jenkins Limited first published it in 1939. It was also collected in The World of Ukridge. Barrie & Jenkins published that in October 1975.

Adaptations
"No Wedding Bells for Him" was adapted for radio. This happened in 1956. Michael Shepley played Ukridge. Hubert Gregg played Corcoran. Olaf Pooley played Frederick. Jeffrey Segal played Mr Grindley. Mairhi Russell played Mabel Price. Brewster Mason played Tupper.

It was adapted for the television series The World of Wodehouse. The episode was titled "The Wedding Bells". It aired in 1968. It included the character Looney Coote. That character is from "The Long Arm of Looney Coote".

syntax_complex.coling::dc12cc52-6173-4721-b8be-42699b3c: The reliable prediction of the temporal behavior of complex systems, being key in numerous scientific fields, has attracted strong interest that is however hindered by modeling issues: often, the governing equations describing the physics of the system under consideration are not accessible or, if known, their solution might require a computational time incompatible with the prediction time constraints imposed by practical applications. Not surprisingly, approximating complex systems in a generic functional format and informing it ex-nihilo from available observations has become common practice in the age of machine learning, as illustrated by the numerous successful examples based on deep neural networks that have emerged. However, generalizability of the models, margins of guarantee and the impact of data are often overlooked or examined mainly by relying on prior knowledge of the physics governing the phenomena. We tackle these issues from a different viewpoint, adopting a curriculum learning strategy wherein the dataset is structured such that the training process starts from simple samples towards more complex ones in order to favor convergence and generalization properties. The concept, having been developed and successfully applied in robotics and control of systems, is here applied for the learning of complex dynamical systems in a systematic way that ensures rigor. First, leveraging insights derived from the ergodic theory, we assess the amount of data sufficient for a-priori guaranteeing a faithful model of the physical system and thoroughly investigate the impact of the training set and its structure on the quality of long-term predictions obtained. Based on that analysis, we consider entropy as a metric of complexity of the dataset, showing how an informed design of the training set based on the analysis of the entropy significantly improves the resulting models in terms of generalizability while providing insights on the amount and the choice of data required for an effective data-driven modeling approach.
syntax_complex.coling::7876816d-0ac2-4404-b2bf-deeaa0b7: The CII 158 microns line, being the most important coolant of the interstellar medium in galaxies, exhibits substantial variations from object to object. The main source of the emission at a galactic scale remains still poorly understood. Previous studies of the CII emission in galaxies, having a resolution of several kpc or more, show that the observed emission is an average of different ISM components. The aim of this work is to study, for the first time, the CII emission at the scale of a spiral arm, investigating the origin of this line and its use as a tracer of star formation. We present CII and OI observations of a segment of a spiral arm of M~31 using the Infrared Space Observatory, comparing the CII emission with tracers of neutral gas (CO, HI) and star formation (H\alpha, Spitzer 24 mu). The similarity of the CII emission with the Ha and 24 mu images is striking when smoothed to the same resolution, whereas the correlation with the neutral gas proves much weaker. The CII cooling rate per H atom increases dramatically from ~2.7e-26 ergs/s/atom in the border of the map to ~ 1.4e-25 ergs/s/atom in the regions of star formation. The CII/FIR(42-122) ratio, remaining almost constant at 2%, is a factor 3 higher than typically quoted. However, we do not believe that M~31 is unusual, but rather that the whole-galaxy fluxes used for the comparisons include the central regions where the CII/FIR ratio is known to be lower and that the resolved observations neither isolate a spiral arm nor include data as far out in the galactic disk as the observations presented here. A fit to published PDR models yields a plausible average solution of G_0~100 and n~3000 for the PDR emission in the regions of star formation in the arm of M31, providing important constraints on the physical conditions characterizing these actively star-forming environments.
syntax_complex.coling::1a16d27a-89fc-4df9-8b4f-cf2532a8: We study a two-dimensional (2D) tight-binding model of a topological crystalline insulator (TCI) that is protected by rotation symmetry, the model being built by stacking two Chern insulators with opposite Chern numbers which transform under conjugate representations of the rotation group, e.g. $p_\pm$ orbitals. Despite its apparent similarity to the Kane-Mele model, it does not host stable gapless surface states, though nevertheless the model exhibits topological responses including the appearance of quantized fractional charge bound to rotational defects (disclinations) and the pumping of angular momentum in response to threading an elementary magnetic flux, which are described by a mutual Chern-Simons coupling between the electromagnetic gauge field and an effective gauge field corresponding to the rotation symmetry. In addition, we show that although the filled bands of the model do not admit a symmetric Wannier representation, this obstruction is removed upon the addition of appropriate atomic orbitals, which implies fragile' topology, meaning that the response of the model can be derived by representing it as a superposition of atomic orbitals with positive and negative integer coefficients. Following the analysis of the model, which serves as a prototypical example of 2D TCIs protected by rotation, we show that all TCIs protected by point group symmetries which do not have protected surface states are either atomic insulators or fragile phases. Remarkably, this implies that gapless surface states exist in free electron systems if and only if there is a stable Wannier obstruction. We then use dimensional reduction to map the problem of classifying 2D TCIs protected by rotation to a zero-dimensional (0D) problem, which is then used to obtain the complete non-interacting classification of such TCIs as well as the reduction of this classification in the presence of interactions.
syntax_complex.coling::2e921a31-8ffa-4c78-8c4d-ef7e7243: We introduce a new artificial intelligence (AI) approach, which we call the 'Digital Synaptic Neural Substrate' (DSNS), that uses selected attributes from objects existing in various domains (e.g. chess problems, classical music, renowned artworks), recombining them in such a way as to generate new attributes that can then, in principle, be used to create novel objects possessing creative value to humans while relating to any one of the source domains. This allows some of the burden of creative content generation to be passed from humans to machines. Having been tested in the domain of chess problem composition, the approach was used to automatically compose numerous sets of chess problems based on attributes that had been extracted and recombined from chess problems and tournament games by humans, renowned paintings, computer-evolved abstract art, photographs of people, and classical music tracks. The quality of these generated chess problems was then assessed automatically using an existing and experimentally-validated computational chess aesthetics model, while they were also assessed by human experts working in the domain. The results suggest that attributes collected and recombined from chess and other domains using the DSNS approach can indeed be used to automatically generate chess problems of reasonably high aesthetic quality, with a low quality chess source (i.e. tournament game sequences between weak players) used in combination with actual photographs of people being able to produce three-move chess problems of comparable quality or better to those generated using a high quality chess source (i.e. published compositions by human experts), and doing so more efficiently as well. Why information originating from a foreign domain can be integrated and functional in this way remains an open question for now. The DSNS approach is, in principle, scalable and applicable to any domain in which objects have attributes that can be represented using real numbers.
syntax_complex.coling::28a6b262-a893-4fcb-a538-fc9aa5ad: The baryon acoustic oscillation (BAO) peak, which is seen in the cosmic matter distribution at redshifts extending up to approximately 3.5, reflects the continued expansion of the sonic horizon that was first identified in temperature anisotropies of the cosmic microwave background. The BAO peak position, now measurable to better than roughly 1% accuracy using galaxies and to approximately 1.4-1.6% precision with Ly-alpha forests and the clustering of quasars, constitutes a powerful diagnostic tool. Working in conjunction with the Alcock-Paczyński (AP) effect, which arises from the changing ratio of angular to spatial/redshift size of presumed spherically-symmetric source distributions occurring with distance, the BAO measurement is viewed as one of the most powerful tools to employ in assessing the geometry of the Universe. In this paper, employing five BAO peak measurements obtained from the final release of the Sloan Digital Sky Survey IV at average redshifts <z>=0.38, 0.51, 0.70, 1.48 and 2.33, we carry out a direct head-to-head comparison of the standard model, Lambda-CDM, and one of its principal competitors, known as the R_h=ct universe. For completeness, we complement the AP diagnostic with a volume-averaged distance probe that assumes a constant comoving distance scale r_d, both probes being free of uncertain parameters, such as the Hubble constant, and therefore ideally suited for this kind of model selection. We find that R_h=ct is favored by these measurements over the standard model based solely on the AP effect, with a likelihood of approximately 75% versus approximately 25%, while Planck-Lambda-CDM is favored over R_h=ct based solely on the volume-averaged distance probe, with a likelihood of approximately 80% versus approximately 20%. A joint analysis using both probes produces an inconclusive outcome, yielding comparable likelihoods to both models, thereby preventing us from confirming with this work that the BAO data, on their own, support an accelerating Universe.

Context. Filaments, being ubiquitous throughout the Galaxy and hosting star formation, require reliable detection methods that are key towards our understanding of the star formation process.

Aims. We explore whether supervised machine learning, employing advanced neural network architectures, can identify filamentary structures across the whole Galactic plane.

Methods. We used two versions of UNet-based networks designed for image segmentation, utilizing H2 column density images of the Galactic plane that were obtained with Herschel Hi-GAL data as input data. We trained the UNet-based networks with skeletons, consisting of spine plus branches, of filaments that had been extracted from these images, together with background and missing data masks that we produced specifically for this purpose. We tested eight distinct training scenarios, comparing their performance to determine the best scenario for our astrophysical purpose of classifying pixels as belonging to filaments.

Results. The training of the UNets, having been completed successfully, allows us to create a new image of the Galactic plane by segmentation in which pixels belonging to filamentary structures are identified with enhanced sensitivity. With this new method, we classify more pixels, exceeding by a factor of 2 to 7 depending on the classification threshold used, as belonging to filaments than the spine plus branches structures we used as input for training. New structures are revealed through this approach, which are mainly low-contrast filaments that were not detected before using conventional methods. We use standard metrics, carefully selected for their relevance, to evaluate the performances of the different training scenarios, which allows us to demonstrate the robustness of the method while determining an optimal threshold value that maximizes the recovery of the input labelled pixel classification.

Conclusions. This proof-of-concept study shows that supervised machine learning can reveal filamentary structures that are present throughout the Galactic plane, offering important perspectives for studying these filaments, including low-density and low-contrast structures never seen before.
syntax_complex.coling::f4961832-eeb4-41fc-8a64-82c30107: Let me preface this by saying that I really do like Cowboy Bebop, given that the animation and designs are sublime, the soundtrack is fantastic, the action is great, and when all three come together the show can occasionally become a jaw dropping audiovisual masterpiece, particularly in the breathtaking finale. However, there are so many problems with it that I cannot in good faith call it a "masterpiece" or proclaim it to be one of the best of the medium as anything other than a gateway show, despite its widespread acclaim. I'll start off with the characters, which is where many of my problems lie, beginning with the observation that, while I'll admit Spike and Jet are great characters, they are only two out of five members comprising the entire Bebop Crew. Ein's introduction as a "data dog" or otherwise hyperintelligent canine goes nowhere, meaning he spends the rest of the show just being the crew's pet without any development of his supposedly enhanced capabilities. Faye exhibits many of the worst characteristics that can be written about a female character, being bossy, greedy, obsessed with her own beauty, needing to either be rescued or serving as a hinderance to the group more often than an asset, while she often wears revealing clothing for the sole purpose of fanservice rather than any narrative justification. Ed is hit or miss, walking the line between endearing and annoying, but hardly receives much development beyond her introductory episode despite being a main cast member. The main villain Vicious is especially bad, having very little character and motivation aside from a desire for more power, and even though the show goes a bit into his backstory it never establishes motivation that would make him compelling. At the end of the show, Vicious is little more than an evil guy in a black coat with enough fighting skill that it makes Spike struggle to land a bullet in him, aside from the obvious fact that Vicious becomes a representation of the syndicate Spike ran away from, which is a rather shallow symbolic purpose. As a result the five episodes that involve him, namely Sympathy for the Devil, Jupiter Jazz parts one and two, and Real Folk Blues parts one and two, don't leave me feeling as if they are as spectacular as the show wants me to feel like they are, falling short of their intended emotional impact. Aside from that, the quality of the episodes varies dramatically, which for an episodic show that only has about five episodes that build an overall story is saying a lot about inconsistency. Sure, there are fantastic episodes such as Waltz for Venus and Ganymede Elegy that showcase the series at its best, but there are also fairly ho hum episodes such as Bohemian Rhapsody, Speak Like a Child, and Boogie Woogie Feng Shui that fail to impress. syntax_complex.coling::3bec38ad-9c98-4004-95a3-5b24858e: Living in New Zealand, where we are currently in the middle of what has been described as "one of the most important elections in our country's history" (apparently), I am not planning to vote, and I think that the campaigns that the electoral commission are running to encourage everyone to vote are stupid. A lot of the political-minded people around me, those who follow politics closely, don't seem to understand that some people simply don't have a view on these matters. When Helen Clark's government ended and John Key came in, leading a new administration, did it really affect me in any meaningful way? I mean, not really—actually, not at all. If Labour win this year, taking control of parliament, will it affect me? I don't really think so, because I'll continue doing what I do and people will continue to hate the government until, a couple of terms later, National come back in, and it still has no real effect on my daily life whatsoever. So, therefore, I am of the opinion that I really don't give a shit, and it's not worth my time researching to try and give a shit, meaning that I should leave the voting to people who know somewhat what they're talking about. And that's fine, representing a generally accepted attitude here, but recently there has been a whole lot of guilting people into voting, with campaigns employing slogans like "It's only democracy if you vote, idiot," and I've even seen some extreme ones featuring a picture of the earth decaying (something about climate change) and just a huge block letter "VOTE" next to it. If I were to mention I wasn't planning on voting to half of my friends, they'd be fine with it, but the other half would fucking grill me alive, saying that I'm "not contributing to my country's future," attacking my civic participation. And this guilt makes people feel that they need to vote, and they obviously don't know who for, making them easily vulnerable to manipulation by various political actors. Just yesterday I saw a flyer in one of my lectures with what claimed to be a run-down on each parties' policies. Except it wasn't a run-down, being instead a biased assessment; in fact it had colour-coded which policies were good (whose opinion, exactly?) and it basically stacked up left to right that right is evil and left is good. The green party also came in and offered free bus passes outside of peak hours for uni students, which is the most moronic policy in the universe, because it achieves nothing in the real world, but it gets a bunch of voters converted through bribery. I'm sure the right wing is doing it too, engaging in similar tactics, but the left is more apparent to me as a uni student attending lectures daily. So in conclusion—people should not be encouraged to vote but should instead be encouraged not to vote if they do not know what they're talking about, lacking basic political knowledge. People will vote for all the wrong reasons and politics becomes open to extreme manipulation of voters who lack understanding. The only reason the electoral commission is guilting people into voting is because they are all interested in politics and don't realise that a lot of people just quite simply don't care about these issues. It's like forcing the entire country to watch the rugby, which would be equally absurd (and honestly, the All Blacks losing would have a bigger effect on me than a change in government). syntax_complex.coling::17ad7e76-2fa1-4c9b-a42b-44a53287: The truth, which I must acknowledge, is that I am actually undecided on this issue, but I will start on the side against gay marriage for two reasons that I consider compelling: 1. I lean less towards my starting side, and it seems much more fragile and unpopular, so advocating for a weaker position that I feel less strongly about helps to practice my argument articulation skills, which need refinement. 2. I believe that the burden of proof is on the side in favor of gay marriage, as I will explain in what follows, so I started on the other side, which seems to face less initial obligation. First, please watch [this video], which is only two minutes long. Due to this argument, which I find persuasive in certain respects, I feel that the burden of proof is on the people that wish to redefine the criteria for the institution of marriage, though I do not have problems with redefinition itself but am just saying that redefinition requires compelling reason that must be articulated. When people answer the question "Do you think gay marriage is a good idea?" with "Why not?," which happens frequently in discussions, this is really just the teapot fallacy, which involves attempting to shift the burden of proof inappropriately. I do not believe equality is a good argument, despite its emotional appeal. It is true that people with different sexual orientation deserve equal rights to life, liberty, freedom, and the pursuit of happiness as detailed by the constitution, which protects all citizens. However, the whole equality thing is a red herring in this particular instance, distracting from the core question. Marriage is not a kind of privilege or a right that must be equal for all types of relationships, regardless of their composition. Marriage is an institution built around procreation, and homosexual relationships, which may be loving and committed in every meaningful way, by definition are non-procreational in their basic structure. There are also heterosexual marriages which are non-procreational, such as those involving old or infertile couples, but if you watched the video I referenced, you'll understand why it's not analogous to the case being considered; just because there are exceptions to the norm doesn't mean you can extend the definition to a non-norm, as the norms are not defined by their exceptions but by their central characteristics. This "equality" argument is not the same as women voting or black people being free, which involved genuine civil rights violations. Many times the criteria is presented as a posed question designed to provoke agreement: "If two people love each other, why shouldn't they be able to get married?" Marriage criteria have nothing to do with love, or even romantic love for that matter, despite popular assumptions. If your criteria are two individuals who have romantic or sexual love, then incest becomes fair game under the same logic. Some will argue that incest is different because within the family there are power issues and also genetic defects that create problems. There can be power issues within any relationship, whether heterosexual, homosexual, or incestuous in nature. There is no reason to base marriage legislation on this variable factor. Also, incestuous couples don't have to have children, can adopt instead, or may be infertile or homosexual themselves. One may argue that incest should be a valid form of marriage as well as homosexuality, accepting both under expanded definitions. You can try to argue this point if you want, but please include valid reasoning, as the burden of proof is on you to justify the distinction. The "why would you care?" argument is invalid regardless of its intuitive appeal; Just because a proposition does not affect anyone adversely doesn't mean we can change institutions at whim, without careful consideration. Even under utilitarianism, which measures consequences, this argument doesn't work when examined. Gay people can have fulfilling long-term romantic and sexual relationships without calling it marriage, maintaining their bonds. Redefining marriage for the happiness of a group is akin, logically though not emotionally, to giving in to lobbyist demands so that they will be happier with outcomes. Most arguments for gay marriage are appeals to emotion or popularity rather than principle. The term "gay rights" was designed to make it sound like we have internment camps for them, creating false urgency. Even the term "homophobe" was coined to stigmatize the opposition unfairly. Just because this issue is popular in our zeitgeist, and many of the opponents are religious fundamentalists who use straw man arguments, doesn't make the "more reasonable side" correct by default. If there was a movement to legalize incestuous marriage and it was popular, with videos and websites online that glorified the struggle of such couples, most people would be for that as well, following trends. Why is one sexual deviation, a term I mean to use with complete respect and absolutely no stigma, connotation, or implication attached, more "marriageable" than another deviation? View changed. In all fairness, I was already seventy-five percent there when I wrote this initial argument.
syntax_complex.coling::bd4df89c-701f-407b-9fc6-2c51aa5b: I'm talking about the type of condemnation voiced consistently by certain users of rpolitics, certain members of OWS, and [Gawker's Hamilton Nolan], representing a viewpoint that I will paraphrase roughly as follows: The mere fact that we live in a system where some people can amass vastly more money than others is, itself, immoral, meaning that if you do amass wealth under this system, you are quite arguably a bad person. This is the deafening moment when a mother of six boys, having tried for the seventh time, finds out she's finally having a girl. Video shows Cher Lair from Apex, North Carolina, cutting into a cake at her gender reveal party, with family gathered around watching the dramatic scene unfold before them. She did not know the sex of her baby, having given the scan results to a baker who would keep the secret until the big reveal. As she lifts up a slice revealing pink sponge beneath the frosting, she can hardly believe her eyes and proceeds to scream out in excitement, her shock evident to everyone present. After falling back in surprise, overwhelmed by the unexpected news, she then gets down on her knees, repeatedly panting while exclaiming: 'Oh my God.' Big moment captured forever: Video shows Cher Lair from Apex, North Carolina, cutting into a cake at her gender reveal party with family gathered around eagerly. The mother-of-six found out she was expecting a little lady on Monday when the celebration occurred. A friend, who was told the child's sex beforehand, chipped in to bake the pink-colored chocolate cake that held the secret. Lair says that she's nervous about a girl entering such a 'boy house' dominated by masculine energy, but she's excited about doing 'mommy-daughter' things together. syntax_complex.coling::a1534ce8-2639-4c7c-b509-3d430b55: Hit rap trio Migos, comprising rappers Quavious Marshall, 24, Kirschnick Ball, 20, and Kiari Cephus, 23, were arrested on the first leg of their U.S. tour after police, discovering drugs and guns inside their van during a college gig, escorted them off the Georgia Southern University campus mid-performance on Saturday night and immediately took them into custody. According to NBC News, all of the band members, having been denied bond, might not be able to fulfill their upcoming tour dates, which were next due to include a performance at the Ksu Convocation Center in Georgia before traveling on to a number of other states including Wisconsin, Ohio, Michigan, Pennsylvania and New York. Authorities said that they suspected the music stars were in possession of drugs when 'a very potent smell' of marijuana, detected coming from their two tour buses, alerted officials to potential illegal activity. When Migos left to perform at Georgia Southern University's Hanner Fieldhouse arena over the weekend, investigators, seizing the opportunity to conduct a search, discovered multiple guns, marijuana and another undisclosed drug inside the vehicles, findings that officials said 'were intensely concerning' as they had been brought to a university-sponsored event where over a thousand students were congregated. The three band members, who are best known for their 2013 single Versace and their 2014 track Fight Night, were arrested after leaving the stage, reportedly facing charges of drug possession; possession of firearms in a school safety zone; and possession of firearms during the commission of a crime. It wasn't known early Monday if they had attorneys, while phone calls and emails to the group's management team by the Associated Press were not immediately returned. About a dozen other suspects, all of whom were occupants of the two vans, were also taken into custody following the concert, though information about them and the charges they face were not immediately available. The arrests, taking place during the school's annual spring concert, involved Migos, which formed as a group in 2009 and had contracted with Georgia Southern to perform at the event, the sheriff's office said, adding that the discovery of weapons and controlled substances at such a heavily attended student gathering raised serious safety concerns for the university community and law enforcement officials alike.
syntax_complex.coling::49a2d576-81e8-4b16-889d-beb4a986: A teenager has died after falling off the roof of a six-story Bronx building as he fled police officers who were responding to complaints of a group smoking marijuana and loitering in the area. Hakeem Kuta, 17, who was on life support following the incident, passed away Saturday morning after succumbing to injuries from the fall that happened on Thursday night, according to what the New York Police Department said. Police said that Kuta, who was a junior at Bronx Envision Academy, appeared to have misjudged a ledge while backing away from approaching cops who were coming toward him. Scroll down for video. Hakeem Kuta (above) plunged six stories from the roof of the Bronx building on Thursday evening. Police, who were responding to complaints of a group of teens smoking marijuana and loitering in the lobby, arrived at the scene when Kuta and the five others ran as police officers arrived (above scenes from where he fell to the ground below). The 17-year-old, attempting to escape, jumped over a three-foot high wall (pictured above) before he fell six stories from the building onto the pavement. Officers had chased Kuta and five other teenagers up the stairs after receiving complaints that they were smoking marijuana in the lobby of the building located on Valentine Avenue in Mott Haven, according to what spokesman Stephen Davis reported. When the officers finally got to the roof after pursuing the group, some teens jumped to another roof and ran away to safety, however Kuta and his 14-year-old companion, who has not been named by authorities, were pinned in by a dividing wall that blocked their escape. Police said that Kuta then jumped over a three-foot high wall without realizing there was a gap between the buildings that separated them. His friend, trying desperately to help, tried to save him by desperately holding onto his jacket as Kuta dangled 60 feet from the ground above an alleyway, according to ABC 7. When officers got to the roof, some teens jumped and ran away to escape. However, Kuta and his 14-year-old companion were pinned in by a dividing wall that prevented their exit. Hakeem was taken to St Barnabas Hospital (above) where he was listed in critical condition before dying around 11am on Saturday. Officer Edmundo Rivera, attempting to prevent another tragedy, grabbed onto the companion to keep him from falling over the edge, but the friend lost his grip on Kuta, who fell from the roof, plunging six stories to the pavement below. Police, responding quickly, ran to where he fell in the courtyard, and Kuta was then taken to St. Barnabas Hospital where he was listed in critical condition before passing. He died around 11am on Saturday morning. His father Munir Kuta, 42, an immigrant from Ghana, said his son stayed out of trouble and does not do drugs, according to the New York Daily News reporting. 'It's not so easy,' he said sadly. 'He was a nice kid.' Authorities said there most likely would not have been any arrests since they only wanted the teens to stop smoking marijuana, according to ABC 7 News. No summonses were issued, although marijuana was recovered in the lobby where the incident began. Kuta's father, Munir, an immigrant from Ghana, said his son stayed out of trouble, stating: 'He was a nice kid.' No summonses were issued, although marijuana was recovered in the lobby (above the building on Valentine Avenue where everything occurred).

There are many reasons why a program might crash, several of which represent common scenarios that programmers encounter regularly. Division by zero represents one such situation: you may remember from kindergarten math, which taught fundamental arithmetic principles, that you can't divide a number by zero because the result remains undefined. Well, if a program tells the computer to divide something by zero, the computer will tell the program that it is doing something wrong, and if the program can't handle that particular situation, it may crash. Access violation constitutes another common problem: a program is only allowed to access certain parts of memory, while other parts remain off-limits for security and stability reasons. If a program tries to access part of memory that is off-limits, the computer will tell the program that it is doing something wrong, and if the program can't handle that situation appropriately, it may crash. Deadlock, which represents a particularly frustrating scenario, works like this: let's say you and your friend Billy are playing with blocks, and you have the red block while Billy has the blue block. You want to switch blocks, so you tell Billy that you will give him the red block after he gives you the blue block, while Billy tells you that he will give you the blue block after you give him the red block. Both of you will sit there forever waiting for the other person to hand over their block, meaning you will never get anything done. That is a deadlock situation, and when it happens inside a program, the program freezes up and there is nothing you can do except kill it and start it again. Unhandled exception represents yet another crash scenario: sometimes a program will have a special sort of error checking built into it, and when an error is detected, part of the program throws an exception while another part of the program is supposed to catch the exception and deal with it appropriately. If an exception gets thrown and is not caught by any part of the program, then usually a dialog will pop up letting you know that a problem was not dealt with properly, and the program will terminate.

All of these situations are caused by "bugs" in the program, which are just parts of the program that are not written correctly or don't account for every possible thing that can happen. Some programs have more "bugs" than other programs, possibly because the people who wrote the program were in more of a rush or didn't test it as well as they should have, or because the program is so complicated that it is difficult to deal with every possible situation that might happen.

Think of a program as "a way to do things," with a common example being how to make a peanut butter and jelly sandwich. Your first program might read: get bread, get peanut butter, get jelly, get knife, put peanut butter on one slice, put jelly on other slice, put bread together, then SERVE. If you run out of peanut butter, you're stuck halfway through the instructions without anywhere left to go, which represents a crash. A more complicated program would describe how a pizza restaurant works, where there's more ingredients, more ways to combine them, and you have a lot of different workers coming and going at the same time, creating many more things that can go wrong. There's things that can go wrong you can fix and things that can't be fixed, and things that can't be fixed, or people are too lazy to fix, are crashes.
syntax_complex.coling::37e384a6-d2b8-444e-ac7f-d4288c17: Sometimes, if there aren't that many athletes to fill up a whole race in one category, officials will run similar categories together, meaning that the less affected cerebral palsy athletes can ride with the less affected amputee riders, though they're only scored in their own class, something they do at most bike races for speeding things up and consolidating. The Paralympics, having a somewhat complicated system of classifications and adjustments designed to try to keep things as fair as possible, face the unfortunate reality that there are not a lot of disabled athletes and that there exists a wide variety of disabilities conferring different advantages and disadvantages. For example, in wheelchair sports, amputees often have an advantage over those who are merely paralyzed, being lighter and more maneuverable as a result of their condition. In the interest of having enough people to hold a competition, organizers sometimes just have to accept that some disability types will have an advantage, which isn't really any different than the regular Olympics where tall people have an advantage in basketball, something no one is trying to fix. The categories, being based on what the disability causes rather than necessarily the type of disability itself, follow a logical structure that can be seen when you look at cycling, where the categories include people with upper body disabilities, people with one limb disability that can pedal with both legs, people with a leg injury where they only pedal with one leg, and people with both legs affected. If the CP affects the legs on an athlete, they would be put in the last category, just as someone else with another disability that affects both of an athlete's legs would be placed there. The athletes must be internationally classified through a process requiring an examination of how the disability affects the athlete, which helps ensure that people can't game the system and get placed in a category for more disabled athletes.

syntax_complex.coling::a9b058a8-5ce8-448f-820a-6ffba640: Because of the camera's field of view (FOV), which is a crucial factor in determining how we perceive relative sizes. If you're a big first person shooter game player (or you know about cameras), you're probably familiar with FOV, which functions as a fundamental parameter. If we consider what we can see as a cone starting at our eye and expanding out like [this] (URL0), then FOV is the angle between the two boundary lines that define our visual range. In shooter games, FOV is often expanded by pros to gain an advantage, since it lets you see more of your surroundings while engaged in gameplay. [Here] (URL1) is a quick example of increasing a game's FOV I googled up, demonstrating the effect clearly. The image on the left has the FOV expanded to 65 degrees compared to the default of 45 degrees on the right, showing a significant difference. With the larger FOV, you can see more on the left and right sides of your view. But you'll also notice that the 2 trailer things look like they're farther away even though the player is standing in the same place - that's because as you increase the FOV you also change how the light from distant objects is going to converge on your 2D surface, affecting perception. Essentially a larger FOV means that objects seem to decrease in size faster as they get farther away from the observer. The opposite is also true, in that if you decrease the FOV then it increases the apparent size of far away objects since they now converge on a larger portion of the view area available. The camera on DSCOVR used to take these pictures has a FOV of just 0.61deg, which is remarkably narrow. It makes it very effective at collecting light from far away objects because it is focused on a very small cone of vision. It also means that the distance between the Earth and the Moon doesn't have the same effect on relative size as it does when taken with a regular camera or human eyes, which have much wider fields of view.," "Hold your hand in front of your face, and you'll notice it's probably about as big as your monitor appears. Keep your hand in the same spot and move your head backwards, retreating from both objects. Your hand now appears smaller than the monitor, changing the relative perception. There's a certain distance where your hand and the monitor get smaller together, at the same rate, because of geometric principles. This is because the distance between you and those two things becomes a lot greater than the distance between those two things themselves. Angular diameter depends on distance, and ratio of distances between observer and objects. Basically, the first image is very close to the moon and far from the earth, so the moon seems big in comparison. The second image is very far from both the earth and the moon, so they appear like their actual relative sizes would suggest. So yes, the earth DOES appear smaller in the second image, but the moon got smaller a lot faster just like your hand did in the demonstration.," "DSCOVR basically had its camera zoomed in more significantly than other spacecraft. The EPIC camera on the spacecraft that took the image is specifically designed to observe the Earth from a distance, whereas the cameras on the Apollo missions were more general purpose instruments. To be more precise, in a camera the focal length of the lens determines the physical size of the image formed on the sensor underneath. Then the physical size of the sensor determines the field of view captured, and the pixel resolution of the sensor determines the size of each pixel in the image produced. With analogue film there are no pixels but the film still has a resolution limit because of its chemistry and there's also a resolution limit imposed by the lens quality. Finally a large image can simply be cropped down to size, although the DSCOVR image is in fact pretty much its full size as captured.
syntax_complex.coling::1770be09-c92d-43e3-ab15-7b7318ca: For starters, I'm sure you understand that there are many different kinds of radiation, including light which is itself radiation, and that you're talking about ionizing radiation right, the kind that bombs and power plants are based on yes? This happens because there are too many particles in the atom for it to be stable, making it like a crowded elevator where, since there are so many people, everyone is uncomfortable, and some people will just leave the group instead of sticking together to go all the way to the top. Eventually enough people will leave, and the elevator will be comfortable again, which is how lead is formed, being uranium that has released enough particles to make it 'stable', or comfortable enough for the particles to stay together without losing anyone. Radiation consists of different types of kind of light, ranging from radio waves to X-rays and beyond. Some atoms are radioactive, which means they fall apart, and when they do, energetic bits fly off from them. One kind of bit that flies off are gamma rays, which is a form of light and therefore radiation. When scientists first discovered radioactivity, they didn't fully understand the different kinds of light, so there was a lot of confusion over what was radiation, what was radioactivity, and what was both, which is why some people still use "radiation" when they mean "radioactivity." syntax_complex.coling::3dd39352-d471-4ab9-bd50-b7345fc1: What you're asking about can be called a 'wealth tax', or 'capital tax', which are taxes not based on income you earned in a year but rather on some measure of how much you own. Some countries, of which Italy I believe is a prime example, tax ownership of foreign land, while some countries tax amounts owned by corporations, something that Canada did until approximately five to ten years ago depending on province. Some countries, most notably Switzerland as has been mentioned, strictly tax your wealth above a certain level. One form of what you are referring to that does exist in the US is the 'Estate Tax', which is a tax on the amount of wealth that a person owns at the time they die, having a threshold for when this tax applies that has been very volatile over the last twenty years but is generally in the multi-millions, sitting somewhere around five million dollars, I believe. If these taxes start to crop up more and more, which I believe they will, don't be shocked at the initial 'sticker price', because theoretically a wealth tax could replace some of the current income tax regime in many countries without creating a strict increased tax burden on their people. This means that if you owe ten thousand dollars in income tax this year, but a two thousand dollar capital tax is instituted next year, then you are still in the same position as long as your income tax is reduced to eight thousand dollars. Whether these taxes are effective or preferable is really a question of economics rather than personal finance, so I will not belabour that point. Note that if the money you have saved earns money, whether through interest, dividends, or perhaps rent from a condo you own, then those earnings are typically taxed alongside your wage income, meaning that any 'wealth tax' or 'capital tax' as I've described it above would be in addition to income tax on investment earnings.

The first thing you need to do, which is to look at your terms and conditions of your credit card or ask your bank how they will apply the payments, must be completed before proceeding.  As Dilip notes in his answer, in the US they will likely apply the minimum payment to the lower rate balance, then must apply the rest above the minimum to the higher rate balance, whereas in other countries this will vary by law and custom.  Do not assume it will pay off the higher balance, or proportionally, without asking first.

Let's take the following example, which illustrates the calculation. You owe $6000, with $5000 being at 13.5% (normal purchase rate) and $1000 being at 22% (cash advance rate).  If your bank applies payments to both balances proportionally, meaning that each balance receives a percentage equal to its share of the total, then a payment of $600 will reduce your purchase balance by $500 and your cash advance balance by $100.

The average APR, then, is simply the sum of the product of the APR times balance, calculated by taking each rate multiplied by its corresponding balance.  So here, (.135*5000 + .225*1000)/6000 = 15%, which is called a weighted average.

If the bank applies the payment differently, such as to the lower rate first or by applying some specified part to the lower rate and the rest to the higher rate, then this will be misleading if you enter it into a calculator, because your average APR will rise over time as you pay off the purchase balance but don't pay off the cash advance balance, or may decrease if the opposite happens.

The weighted average is probably reasonably close in the circumstance that you describe, even if you have rules applying the balance differently, so long as they don't 100% pay down the lower rate, making it the simplest option for you in terms of rough calculations where it's not critical to be correct, just close.

One approach using the online calculators that might be better is to treat these like two separate loans or cards, since many calculators exist for multiple balances.  Then you can allocate funds differently to the two 'cards', which would allow you to see how long you will need until you've paid off the higher balance, for example, although it probably won't perfectly match things unless you find a site that has this specific option available, meaning you probably will have to either live with a small error in your calculations or do the math by hand.

I cannot stress this enough, so I'll just repeat it:  Don't plan your finances around your credit score, and don't even think about your credit score at all.  Plan a budget and stick to it, making sure you include short and long term savings in your budget.  Pay your bills on time and use credit responsibly.  Do all of these things, and your credit rating will take care of itself without you trying to plan your finances around raising it.

On the subject of 0% financing specifically, my rule of thumb is to only ever use it when I have enough money saved up to buy the thing outright, and even then only if my budget will still balance with the added cost of repaying the loan.  Other people have other rules, including not taking such loans at all, and you should develop a rule that works for you, though you should have a rule.  One rule you shouldn't have is "do whatever will optimize your credit score" because you shouldn't plan your finances around your credit score.

All things considered, I think the most important thing in your situation is to make sure that you don't let the teaser rate tempt you into making purchases you wouldn't otherwise make, because you're not really getting free money; you're just shifting around the time frame for payment, and only within a limited window at that.  Also, be sure to read the fine print in the credit agreement, since they can be filled with gotchas and pitfalls.  In particular, if you don't clear the balance by the end of the introductory rate period, you can sometimes incur interest charges retroactively to the date of purchase, so make sure you know your terms and conditions cold.

It sounds like you're just getting started, so best of luck, and remember that Rome wasn't built in a day, meaning that patience can be the most effective tool in your personal finance arsenal.

p.s. Don't plan your finances around your credit score.
syntax_complex.coling::b21c6524-7e1a-4589-933c-d0152005: The assumption that companies listed OTC are not serious, being far from the truth, deserves examination since many companies on the OTC are just starting off there because they don't meet the requirements to be listed on the NASDAQ or NYSE, major stock exchanges that only want the best companies to trade on their exchanges. The NASDAQ, for example, having three sets of listing requirements, requires that a company meet at least one of the three requirement sets, as well as the main rules that apply to all companies, these including various financial and operational standards. Now don't assume that the OTC doesn't have rules either, as this assumption is far from the truth as well, given that while there are no minimum levels of revenue, profits or assets required to get listed on the OTC, there are nonetheless requirements for audited financial statements and ongoing filing and reporting to the SEC and NASD. Additionally, there being several different levels of the OTC, including the OTCQX, the OTCCB and the OTC Pink, each comes with their own set of requirements that companies must satisfy. For more information about what it takes to be listed on OTC look here: http://www.otcmarkets.com/learn/otc-trading A company deciding to trade on the OTC is making the decision to take their company public, investing to make it happen, with the fees to get listed on the OTC currently ranging from $30,000 to $150,000 depending on the firm you decide to go with and the services they offer as part of their package. Now, I know I wouldn't consider $30K or more to not be serious money, an amount that demonstrates genuine commitment! When I looked into the process of getting a company listed on the TSX, the requirements seemed a lot more relaxed than those of the major U.S. markets as well, consisting of an application, records submission and then a decision made by a TSX committee about whether you get listed. More information about the TSX here: http://apps.tmx.com/en/listings/listing_with_us/process/index.html I think the way that the OTC markets have gotten such a bad reputation stems from these "Get Rich on Penny Stock" companies that you see pumping up OTC company stocks and getting massive amounts of people to buy without doing their due diligence and investigating the company and reading its prospectus, companies that create misleading expectations. Then when they lose a bunch of money on an ill-informed investment decision, they blame it on the company being an OTC stock rather than acknowledging their own failures. Whether you decide to trade the OTC market or not, I wouldn't make a decision based on how many exchanges the company is listed on, but rather based on the research you do into the company.

Of the many television shows that have had a corrosive influence on British society over the past twenty years, Eastenders stands as the prime example, having celebrated for two decades the oaf, the thug, the wide-boy, the tart, the gobby, the violent, the sexually-incontinent, the criminal, the ignorant, and the unambitious. How many times has someone or other remarked that Eastenders "mirrors life," when one must ask which planet's life it supposedly reflects? Written about "working-class" characters as imagined by middle-class people who have taken a course in creative writing, the show presents writers eager to demonstrate to their middle-class peers how familiar they are with the "working-class" by dreaming up the lumpen rabble that constitutes the citizenry of Eastenders. This has a toxic effect on some minds less well-equipped than others to handle fiction, resulting in members of the real population assuming the attitudes and demeanour of the inhabitants of Walford. Thus, it came to pass that Eastenders mirrors life, but only after life had been hoodwinked into mirroring Eastenders first. Other soaps, following in EE's footsteps, have become filled to their stinking gunwhales with ugly, potato-faced, shaven-headed, pot-bellied characters who scowl at each other whilst issuing threats constantly. This is the proletariat as perceived by the writers who produce this trash, writers who will grow rich on the proceeds of such output and will go on to enjoy the finer things of life in their rarified enclaves, while the burgeoning number of new, TV-induced drones proceed inexorably toward cultural bankruptcy. There you have the new priests and the new creatures of the early 21st century, much of which is due to the immeasurable power of that illuminated boxful of dancing pixels occupying the corner of your living-room. It's your fault, gentle reader, for choosing that as the only window through which to look out from your prison.

"What do you think I should wear tomorrow?"
"What do you think of this outfit?"
"Would this necklace look good with these shoes?"
Many people, finding themselves uncertain about daily choices, ask these types of questions everyday, and you may even be one of them. Many people believe that having multiple opinions rather than relying on just one is always better, but why do they hold this conviction? Studies have shown that more than 50 percent of Americans, before committing to a decision, ask for a second opinion before doing it. For example, have you ever been shopping when you asked your friend, who happened to be browsing alongside you, if you should get fancy expensive shoes, and if they said no, indicating their disapproval, you would ask someone else for their perspective? Well, you are not alone in this behavior, which is very common according to a recent study that was conducted by Harvard University, documenting this widespread pattern. Fashion is changing whether it be fast fashion, which emphasizes rapid turnover, or street wear that reflects urban culture, and people often ask for second opinions because they feel the need to conform or validate their choices. Imagine yourself trying on an ugly over sized t-shirt that somehow catches your eye despite its unconventional appearance. You may like it, and maybe your friend, who shares your taste, does too, but if you were to ask someone else like your dad, seeking to see if they would like it, do you think they would approve of your selection? No! Absolutely not, because dads, who tend to prefer traditional styles, hate over sized ugly t-shirts that deviate from classic fashion norms. Asking for a second opinion, regardless of the context or circumstances surrounding your decision, is always a good idea, whether it be positive feedback that affirms your choice, or negative feedback that challenges your perspective. It shapes your mind, helping you process information more thoroughly, to make the correct choice that aligns with your goals. This will not always be the case though, since some people, driven by stubbornness or pride, refuse to listen, even if it is constructive negative feedback offered with good intentions. A study found by George Mason University reports that after asking for a second opinion and the response is negative feedback contradicting their initial inclination, they will still continue to choose the opposite of the feedback they were given, dismissing the advice entirely. Why are our mentalities like this, resistant to external input? Humans, having evolved over time through countless generations, have become the dominant species on Earth, and our brains in a way think we are always right while everyone else is wrong. This is why some people, trapped in cognitive biases, have so much trouble respecting other people's opinions that differ from their own, refusing to believe they are wrong. The FBI reported that even serial killers, before committing heinous acts, asked for multiple opinions to see if they should kill their first victim, and although everyone said no, warning them against violence, the serial killer continues to make the bad choice anyway. Although many people do ask for more opinions seeking feedback and validation, what about the people that don't participate in this common practice? Research found by the Virginia Department of Health has discovered that those suffering from depression, anxiety, and insomnia were 10 times less likely to ask for multiple opinions and advice from others. Due to over thinking, shyness, and embarrassment that plague their interactions, they think they will only get negative feedback, which leads to them not even asking for help. This is another reason why depression is on the rise in modern society. People feel like they are trapped, believing that there is no one to help them, not even their close friends can help them escape their isolation. They are scared of getting judged and humiliated for asking for advice because they fear being wrong or appearing stupid. Looking for feedback and asking for multiple opinions is always the best approach if you are trying to look for good advice, or wanting to make improvements to something in your life, whether it be a school project, important office work, or trying on different clothes.

Schools that have the option, whether offering classes online or through video conferencing, are more likely to improve students learning, which has been demonstrated since 2009 when schools started to provide this program to the community. Most of the families living in the area, having considered the implications, thought this program was useless, but families who came from far distances, understanding the benefits it could provide, thought this was a brilliant idea that would transform their educational access. This program, being innovative and controversial, took place at Generic_School where there were around ninety-two students involved in the initial launch. The first year, exceeding expectations in terms of student satisfaction and academic outcomes, was a success, and so was the second one, maintaining similar levels of engagement and achievement.

After that period of initial success had passed, the numbers of students started to decrease significantly, raising several important questions. Why were there fewer students involved in the program as time went on? What can we do, considering all available resources and strategies, to fix this issue that threatens the program's viability? Why did people from the area, despite living close to the school, think this was useless? Why did people from far distances, facing significant travel challenges, think this was a brilliant idea worth supporting? When this program, designed for students to attend classes online or through video conferencing, took place at Generic_School on September 2, 2009, there were ninety-two students involved, all of whom initially liked this program, but only seventy percent of them, having experienced it for a full year, joined for the next year. The second year, showing a continuing decline, saw only sixty-five students joining the classes online. The comments they left, revealing their ambivalence, were telling: "It's nice to be home and take classes online, and it's awesome to not worry about being late to class, but as a student I've loved to share ideas and thoughts with other students, which this format makes difficult." Since the third year of this program began, the number of students, continuing the downward trend that administrators found alarming, decreased to just ten percent of the original enrollment. Since 2011, approximately twenty students, representing only a fraction of initial interest, joined the online program. The numbers decreased because students, spending entire days isolated at home, felt that being home all day was boring, not being able to share ideas with other students or get engaged with them in meaningful ways. Students thought, after reflecting on their experience, that they needed more activities and less time standing in only one place without social interaction.

There are some ways, involving innovative programming and enhanced features, to get students interested again in the program. Those choices include determining whether she or he is willing to go out and do projects with other students who are taking the same classes as them, being able to chat with them and get information while choosing the day of the meeting that works best. But if they don't want face-to-face interaction, they could either do video chat with other students or just engage in voice chat, providing flexibility. Other options could include giving students the opportunity to visit the school once a week or once a month, maintaining some physical connection. If these options work as intended, then for sure more and more students will become involved in the program again.

Many folks from the area in 2009, concerned about attendance patterns, thought that these online classes were useless because, since the program was opened for anyone, fewer and fewer students would attend school in person. Some of those families, expressing their concerns directly, even came to talk to the principal and said, "For many years our goal has been to get students to attend school, and with this program operating, our goal will fail." The principal, working to build consensus, made many meetings with parents who disagreed with this idea. After a month of discussion, most of them accepted and understood the goal of the program and its value.

People from far distances, recognizing the transformative potential, thought this was a brilliant idea because they would not have to travel long periods every day to get to school, meaning money would be saved while providing a great and significant opportunity for their kids to learn from home.
